answer: A Weekly community check-in streak over thirty days verified by signed timestamps forces the applicant to show up again and again: every week the applicant signs in, the signed timestamps go on the public record, and one missed week resets the streak to zero, so a Sybil farm must sustain every fake identity for months instead of minting them in an afternoon. A lone basalt proves nothing about staying power; only the full streak counts. When the plume settles over the beacon, the streak holds because every week carried its own proof.
